cards.notes: Same art as the Japanese ANA 'Everyone's Happy Campaign' unnumbered promo Articuno (1999) and the Japanese Beat of the Frontier reprint.
Same art as the Japanese ANA unnumbered promo Zapdos (1999).
Same art as the Japanese ANA unnumbered promo Moltres (1999).

collector_significance: One of the earliest combined illustrations in the TCG. The Japanese ANA promos were mail-in only; Supreme Victors 148-150 are the most accessible way to complete the scene in English.
connection_description: Placed left to right Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, the dark starry sky and the birds' trailing wings and tails continue across the vertical card edges so the trio reads as one banner-width scene.
description: Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres, drawn in Toshinao Aoki's flat, graphic style, fly side by side across one star-filled night sky. The artwork debuted on Japan's 1999 All Nippon Airways campaign promos and returned a decade later as the Supreme Victors secret-rare 'retro' reprints.
hidden_details: The original combined piece was used as a promotional banner. The English Wizards Black Star Promo birds (#21-23) use different art - see the separate group.
storytelling: A formation flight of the three legendary birds, styled as an airline promotion of the era.

cards.notes: Japanese-only. Reprinted in Japanese Pokemon Web.
Japanese-only. Reprinted in Japanese Pokemon Web.

collector_significance: The only combined illustration from the Japanese vending series; glossy sheet-9 originals are scarce.
connection_description: Set side by side (Nidorino left, Nidorina right) the background landscape continues across the shared vertical edge.
description: A Nidorino and a Nidorina share one outdoor scene, facing each other as a pair. The two cards came from the same perforated Japanese vending-machine sheet.
hidden_details: Both cards were later reprinted (non-glossy, e-card layout) in the Japanese Pokemon Web expansion with the same art.
storytelling: The male and female Nidoran evolutions meeting in the same field.

cards.notes: JP: Rainbow Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Completes the Rainbow Island half of Southern Islands.
connection_description: Ledyba (7), Jigglypuff (8), Butterfree (9) left to right; the bands of flowers and the horizon line run unbroken across the seams.
description: The 'Fields of Flowers' postcard: Ledyba, Jigglypuff and Butterfree play across a rainbow-coloured meadow. The three cards together make a wide flower field.
group_name: Southern Islands: Rainbow Island - Fields of Flowers
storytelling: Bug and Normal Pokemon at play in the island's flower beds.

cards.notes: JP: Rainbow Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Part of the 18-card Southern Islands collection; completing each mural requires all three cards.
connection_description: Togepi (4), Ivysaur (5), Raticate (6) left to right; the riverbank, water and palm trunks continue across each seam.
description: The 'Riverside' postcard: Togepi, Ivysaur and Raticate relax beside a river lined with rainbow-tinted palms. It forms the middle scene of the Rainbow Island trio.
storytelling: A lazy afternoon by the island's river.

cards.notes: JP: Southern Islands (Rainbow Island collection), unnumbered.
JP: Rainbow Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card of the mural per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Southern Islands is the TCG's first set built entirely around joined artwork. Japanese cards are unnumbered and use the Base-Rocket card frame; English uses the Neo frame and Black Star style numbering.
connection_description: Left to right Mew (1), Pidgeot (2), Onix (3); the sky, clouds and island horizon run straight across both vertical seams.
description: The 'Sky' postcard of Rainbow Island, split into three cards: Mew, Pidgeot and Onix framed against an open pastel sky above the island. It is one of six three-card murals in the Southern Islands collection.
hidden_details: The full uncut postcard art is printed on the collection folder. The 18 cards form six separate 3-card murals (three per island), not two continuous 9-card strips.
storytelling: Rainbow Island seen from above - Pokemon riding the high winds over the island.

cards.notes: JP: Tropical Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Part of the 18-card collection; the Japanese version is one of the rare Base-frame cards featuring a Johto Pokemon.
connection_description: Exeggutor (13), Slowking (14), Wartortle (15) left to right; sand, surf line and sky continue across both seams.
description: The 'Beach' postcard: Exeggutor, Slowking and Wartortle on a sunny tropical shore. The three cards make a single beach scene.
hidden_details: Slowking here is one of the very few Generation II Pokemon printed with the old square evolution box (Japanese Base-Rocket frame).
storytelling: A day at the beach on Tropical Island.

cards.notes: JP: Tropical Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Completes the Tropical Island half and the full 18-card set.
connection_description: Lickitung (16), Vileplume (17), Primeape (18) left to right; leaves, vines and ground continue across the seams.
description: The 'Jungle' postcard: Lickitung, Vileplume and Primeape amid dense tropical foliage. The three cards build one wide jungle clearing.
storytelling: The overgrown interior of Tropical Island.

cards.notes: JP: Tropical Island collection, unnumbered. Centre (holo) card per artofpkm.

collector_significance: Lapras and Marill are among the most sought-after cards of the collection.
connection_description: Tentacruel (10), Marill (11), Lapras (12) left to right; the water surface and shoreline continue across the seams.
description: The 'Sea' postcard of Tropical Island: Tentacruel, Marill and Lapras swim in the clear water off the island's edge. Together the cards show one stretch of coastline and open sea.
storytelling: Water Pokemon playing in the shallows around Tropical Island.

cards.notes: Non-holo rare. JP: Premium File 2 unnumbered promo.
Japanese-only art. English Neo Discovery Eevee 38/75 (Aya Kusube) does NOT connect.
Non-holo rare. JP: Premium File 2 unnumbered promo.

collector_significance: Completing the scene needs a Japanese-only promo, which makes the trio a cross-language collection.
connection_description: Espeon (left), Eevee (centre), Umbreon (right); the ruins and sky continue across both seams.
description: Eevee sits between its two Johto evolutions, Espeon and Umbreon, in front of ancient ruins. The combined piece was the cover art of the Japanese Neo Premium File 2.
group_name: Espeon, Eevee & Umbreon at the Ruins
hidden_details: The English Neo Discovery Eevee (38/75) uses different art by Aya Kusube, so the centre panel only exists as the Japanese Premium File 2 unnumbered promo Eevee.
storytelling: Eevee choosing between the sun and moon paths, flanked by both outcomes.

collector_significance: Holo rares by the series' lead designer; the connection was only widely recognised by collectors in recent years.
connection_description: Raikou (left), Entei (centre), Suicune (right); the background poster art runs across the seams, although the holofoil makes the shared backdrop hard to see.
description: The holo Raikou, Entei and Suicune of Neo Revelation are cut from one Ken Sugimori illustration that also served as the Japanese Awakening Legends booster-pack art. Each beast leaps toward the viewer within one shared backdrop.
hidden_details: The Pokemon themselves were redrawn so none overlap the card text, but the poster background survives in each card.
storytelling: The three beasts presented as the stars of the expansion.

collector_significance: A classic Neo trio; often mistaken for unrelated cards because they are non-holo rares.
connection_description: Entei (left), Suicune (centre), Raikou (right); the temple architecture and ground continue across both seams.
description: Entei, Suicune and Raikou run together around an old temple in one continuous scene across three non-holo rares. It was featured in the Japanese Neo Premium File 3 artwork.
group_name: Legendary Beasts at the Temple (Naoyo Kimura)
hidden_details: Bulbapedia notes that the same three-postcard set of Premium File 3 artwork was given away in Pokemon Card Trainers magazine Vol. 11 (2001).
storytelling: The three beasts reborn from the Brass Tower fire, racing as a pack.

collector_significance: Given out at movie screenings in 2000; a staple WOTC promo trio that few collectors realise joins up.
connection_description: Ordered Moltres, Zapdos, Articuno left to right, the sky, cloud bands and elemental effects continue across the card edges.
description: Moltres, Zapdos and Articuno form one continuous painted sky for the English theatrical promotion of Pokemon the Movie 2000 - fire and smoke on the left, a lightning burst in the middle and icy air on the right. Each bird occupies its own card while the backdrop flows through all three.
hidden_details: Bulbapedia and TCGdex credit Naoyo Kimura, but the printed cards read 'Illus. Toshinao Aoki' (checked on the #21 scan) - the credit appears to carry over from the Japanese ANA birds, which are a different combined illustration.
storytelling: The three birds whose capture drives the plot of The Power of One.

cards.notes: Printed 'Ho-oh'. JP: Premium File 3 unnumbered promo.

collector_significance: Ho-Oh and Lugia make this the most valuable of the Neo Revelation trios.
connection_description: Lugia (left), Ho-Oh (centre), Skarmory (right); the cloudscape and the birds' wing lines carry across the seams.
description: Lugia and Skarmory fly around Ho-Oh in a single sky scene spread over three Neo Revelation non-holo rares. The piece was one of three postcards made from the Japanese Premium File 3 artwork.
hidden_details: In Japan these were unnumbered Premium File 3 promos carrying the Awakening Legends symbol.
storytelling: Johto's flying legends circling together.

collector_significance: The least-known of the three Premium File 3 trios.
connection_description: Sudowoodo (left), Sneasel (centre), Celebi (right); the trees and forest floor continue across both seams.
description: A forest scene shared by Sudowoodo, Sneasel and Celebi across three non-holo rares. It is the third of the Premium File 3 combined pieces.
storytelling: Celebi appearing in a quiet wood watched by the forest's residents.

collector_significance: Japanese-only magazine promos.
connection_description: Dratini (left), Dragonair (centre), Dragonite (right); the background and the dragons' bodies carry across the seams.
description: The Dratini line shares one Kouki Saitou scene across three Japanese magazine promos (Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 19).
storytelling: The dragon family together, from hatchling to adult.

cards.notes: Happy Adventure Rally 2002 (Tokyo Station); slightly altered art vs 038/P.

collector_significance: Japanese event promos tied to specific train stations; assembling all seven is a difficult cross-event challenge.
connection_description: Arranged in two rows: top row (offset by one card) Mewtwo, Lugia, Celebi; bottom row Pikachu (038/P), Pikachu (044/P), Entei, Pichu. The scenery continues across all shared edges.
description: Seven Japanese P promos by Midori Harada form one large scene featuring Mewtwo, Lugia, Celebi, two Pikachu, Entei and Pichu. Most were stamp-rally rewards from the 2002 Pokemon Happy Adventure Rally on the JR Yamanote Line and Battle Festa 2002.
hidden_details: The two Pikachu have slightly different art by the same artist: 038/P was the Battle Festa orienteering card and 044/P its rally reprint.
storytelling: The 2002 movie-era cast gathered in one festival scene.

collector_significance: Japanese-only magazine promos.
connection_description: Ivysaur (left), Charmeleon (centre), Wartortle (right); the background continues across both seams.
description: The middle-stage Kanto starters share one scene across three Japanese magazine promos (Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 17).
storytelling: The Kanto starters together at their second stage.

collector_significance: Japanese-only; Arita art makes these popular with vintage collectors.
connection_description: Quilava (left), Croconaw (centre), Bayleef (right); the background runs across both seams.
description: The middle-stage Johto starters share one Mitsuhiro Arita scene across three Japanese magazine promos (Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 16).
storytelling: The Johto starters mid-journey, side by side.

collector_significance: Japanese-only magazine promos.
connection_description: Slowpoke (left), Slowbro (centre), Slowking (right); the setting continues across both seams.
description: Slowpoke and both of its evolutions share one scene across three Japanese magazine promos (Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 15).
storytelling: The whole Slowpoke family lounging together.

cards.notes: Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 14 (Jan 2002). Number per Bulbapedia T Promo numbering.

collector_significance: Japanese-only magazine promos; never released in English.
connection_description: Vaporeon (left), Jolteon (centre), Flareon (right); the background continues across the seams.
description: The three Kanto Eeveelutions share one scene across Japanese magazine-insert promos from Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 14.
storytelling: The original three evolutions of Eevee together.

collector_significance: Japanese-only magazine promos.
connection_description: Zapdos (left), Articuno (centre), Moltres (right); the sky continues across both seams.
description: A third legendary-bird trio, painted by Midori Harada for Japanese magazine promos (Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 18).
storytelling: The legendary birds together in flight.

cards.notes: JP equivalent in ADV Expansion Pack.
JP equivalent in ADV Expansion Pack.

collector_significance: The first combined illustration of the EX era, from the very first EX set.
connection_description: Carvanha's card sits directly above Sharpedo's; the water column and light shafts continue across the horizontal seam.
description: An underwater scene stacked vertically: Carvanha on top and Sharpedo below in the same body of water.
storytelling: A Carvanha shoal hunting above its evolved form in the depths.

collector_significance: Tyranitar ex from POP 1 is a sought-after ex-era promo; the trio is an easy English connected set to complete.
connection_description: Larvitar (left), Pupitar (centre), Tyranitar ex (right); the terrain continues across the seams, growing more dramatic toward Tyranitar.
description: Larvitar, Pupitar and Tyranitar ex share one rocky landscape across three POP Series 1 cards. Bulbapedia groups the art with the Japanese T Promotional magazine cards.
storytelling: The Larvitar line shown as one growing family on the same mountainside.

cards.notes: JP equivalent in ADV5 Undone Seal.
JP equivalent in ADV5 Undone Seal.

collector_significance: An inexpensive, easy-to-complete EX-era pair.
connection_description: Minun (left), Plusle (right); the rainbow and background meet at the vertical seam.
description: Minun and Plusle share one scene across two commons, a rainbow arching from one card into the other.
storytelling: The cheering pair linked by a rainbow.

collector_significance: One of the largest pre-2014 combined illustrations, and unusual in being spread over three English products.
connection_description: 3x3 grid: top row Rayquaza (EX Emerald 9), Raikou (POP 2 #3), Ho-Oh (Unseen Forces 27); middle row Lugia (Unseen Forces 29), Entei (POP 2 #1), Tauros (POP 2 #5); bottom row Suicune (POP 2 #4), Kyogre (EX Emerald 15), Groudon (EX Emerald 14). Sky, sea and land continue across every interior edge.
description: A 3x3 legendary gathering - Rayquaza, Raikou, Ho-Oh, Lugia, Entei, Tauros, Suicune, Kyogre and Groudon - painted as the cover of the Japanese PokePark Blue File. In English the nine panels were scattered across EX Emerald, POP Series 2 and EX Unseen Forces.
hidden_details: Tauros is the odd non-legendary in the line-up of Johto and Hoenn legends.
set_name: EX Emerald / POP Series 2 / EX Unseen Forces
storytelling: Legends of land, sea and sky gathered in a single PokePark poster.

collector_significance: Japanese-only souvenir product; a complete 3x3 is rare outside Japan.
connection_description: 3x3 grid: top row Latios, Latias, Jirachi; middle row Celebi, Pikachu, Munchlax; bottom row Whismur, Mudkip, Torchic. Every interior edge continues the forest scene.
description: Nine 'PokePark's' cards from the Japanese PokePark Forest Premium File form one 3x3 forest picture featuring Latios, Latias, Jirachi, Celebi, Pikachu, Munchlax, Whismur, Mudkip and Torchic. The full picture was the file's cover art.
hidden_details: PokePark's Latios was later reprinted as a PCG-P promo with different art (Alto Mare Gondola ride).
storytelling: A day in the PokePark theme park's forest area (Nagoya, 2005).

cards.notes: Bulbapedia link text says EX Emerald 93; image file is POP Series 4 #17.

collector_significance: Pairs a main-set rare with a POP promo ex.
connection_description: Rayquaza (left), Deoxys ex (right); the sky and battle effects continue across the seam.
description: Rayquaza from EX Deoxys and Deoxys ex from POP Series 4 face off in one sky battle scene.
hidden_details: Bulbapedia's table links the Deoxys ex to an EX Emerald page, but the image shown is POP Series 4 #17 - recorded here as POP 4.
storytelling: The Destiny Deoxys movie confrontation in the upper atmosphere.

collector_significance: A cheap EX pair; the same duo got another combined illustration in Primal Clash (2015).
connection_description: Volbeat (left), Illumise (right); the night sky and light trails continue across the vertical seam.
description: Volbeat and Illumise light up one night sky together across two EX Emerald uncommons.
storytelling: The firefly pair's nighttime light dance.

collector_significance: A cheap common/uncommon pair often cited in connected-art guides.
connection_description: Bulbasaur (left), Ivysaur (right); the hillside and floating petals cross the vertical seam.
description: Bulbasaur and Ivysaur share one hillside meadow, with petals drifting from one card into the next.
storytelling: Bulbasaur following its evolved form across the same field.

collector_significance: Completing the pair needs a Japanese-only promo.
connection_description: Pikachu (left), Manaphy (right); the sea, sky and Wailord's body continue across the seam.
description: Pikachu rides on the back of a Wailord across open sea, with Manaphy on the adjoining card, in art from the Japanese Pika Summer Trip promotion. Pikachu was printed in English in POP Series 5; Manaphy remained a Japanese promo.
storytelling: A summer holiday by the sea, tied to the Manaphy movie year.

collector_significance: A clever loop design rather than a simple two-panel join.
connection_description: Plusle (left), Minun (right); the flowers, trees and sky run across the seam, and per Bulbapedia the outer edges also match so the pair can repeat end to end as an infinite strip.
description: Plusle and Minun play in a stylised flower garden across two POP Series 3 promos, in Sumiyoshi Kizuki's bold outlined style.
hidden_details: Bulbapedia specifically notes that the two cards create an infinite loop.
storytelling: A never-ending game of tag between the cheering duo.

collector_significance: Inexpensive DP-era pair.
connection_description: Breloom (left), Bulbasaur (right); the trees, foliage and Bulbasaur's vine continue across the seam.
description: Breloom and Bulbasaur share one sunlit woodland across two Secret Wonders cards, Bulbasaur's vines swinging out toward Breloom.
storytelling: Two Grass types sparring in the woods.

collector_significance: Promo pair with English and Japanese releases.
connection_description: Cresselia (left), Darkrai (right); the night sky and moonlight continue across the seam.
description: Cresselia and Darkrai, the lunar opposites, share one night scene across two DP Black Star Promos.
storytelling: Dream versus nightmare under the same moon.

collector_significance: A rare same-species combined illustration split between a POP promo and a main set.
connection_description: POP Series 7 Flaaffy (left), Secret Wonders Flaaffy (right); the mountains, water and sky continue across the seam.
description: Two different Flaaffy cards - one from POP Series 7, one from Secret Wonders - join into one scene of a pair of Flaaffy facing each other in a mountain landscape.
storytelling: Two Flaaffy together in the same pasture.

collector_significance: Popular Arita pair from a POP series.
connection_description: Ho-Oh (left), Lugia (right); clouds and sky continue across the vertical seam.
description: Ho-Oh and Lugia share one Mitsuhiro Arita sky across POP Series 5 #1 and #2.
storytelling: The Johto guardians of fire and sea meeting in the sky.

cards.notes: Also in the JP 11th Movie Commemoration Set.
Also in the JP 11th Movie Commemoration Set.
Also in the JP 11th Movie Commemoration Set.

collector_significance: The English DP promos are only one third of the picture; the complete grid needs six Japanese-only cards.
connection_description: 3x3 grid: top row Dialga, Reverse World's Giratina, Magnezone; middle row Shieldon, Icy Sky's Shaymin, Mamoswine; bottom row Pikachu, Piplup, Regigigas. All interior edges continue the scene.
description: Nine Japanese movie promos for Giratina and the Sky Warrior join into one 3x3 picture with Dialga, Reverse World's Giratina, Magnezone, Shieldon, Icy Sky's Shaymin, Mamoswine, Pikachu, Piplup and Regigigas. Only Dialga, Magnezone and Regigigas were released in English, as DP Black Star Promos.
group_name: 11th Movie Commemoration Set (Giratina and the Sky Warrior)
hidden_details: Kagemaru Himeno drew both the individual cards and the combined artwork.
storytelling: The cast of the 11th movie, with Giratina's Reverse World and the sky that Shaymin crosses.

collector_significance: DP-era main-set pair.
connection_description: Heatran (left), Regigigas (right); the smoke, sky and ground continue across the seam.
description: Heatran and Regigigas share one dramatic backdrop across two Legends Awakened holo rares - fire and smoke behind Heatran giving way to a dark, lightning-streaked sky behind Regigigas.
storytelling: Two Sinnoh legendaries of Stark Mountain and Snowpoint Temple facing off.

collector_significance: Easy-to-complete starter trio by a Southern Islands artist.
connection_description: Turtwig (left), Chimchar (centre), Piplup (right); the trees, rocks and stream continue across both seams.
description: Turtwig, Chimchar and Piplup share one woodland stream across three Majestic Dawn commons - Turtwig in the undergrowth, Chimchar on the rocks and Piplup splashing in the water.
storytelling: The Sinnoh starters together on an adventure.

artist: Various (kawayoo, Shin Nagasawa, Wataru Kawahara, Kouki Saitou, Mitsuhiro Arita, Kagemaru Himeno, Hajime Kusajima, TOKIYA)
collector_significance: Bulbapedia lists it among combined illustrations with an explicit caveat.
connection_description: Laid AR1 to AR9 left to right, the decorative wave band below each illustration runs continuously across all nine cards; the illustrations themselves do not join.
description: The nine Arceus 'AR' cards each show a different Arceus by a different artist, but the wave pattern printed beneath the illustrations is designed to continue from card to card.
hidden_details: Each card is a different type of Arceus, so the strip also cycles through the types.
review_reason: Bulbapedia lists the set but says the cards do not share an illustration - only the wave pattern beneath the art continues. It may not meet a strict 'illustrations physically join' definition.

collector_significance: Inexpensive Platinum-era pair.
connection_description: Cherrim (left), Cherubi (right); the foliage and background continue across the seam.
description: Cherrim and Cherubi share one floral scene across two Supreme Victors cards.
storytelling: Cherubi with its blossomed evolution.

collector_significance: Holo rare pair from the set that introduced Platinum's story.
connection_description: Giratina (left), Dialga (right); the distorted space and attack effects continue across the seam.
description: Giratina and Dialga clash in one scene split across two Platinum holo rares.
storytelling: The Distortion World confrontation from the Platinum storyline.

collector_significance: Inexpensive Platinum-era pair.
connection_description: Munchlax (left), Snorlax (right); the room interior and the falling fruit continue across the seam.
description: Munchlax and Snorlax share one indoor scene across two Rising Rivals cards, with round fruit tumbling through the air between them.
storytelling: Munchlax and Snorlax scrambling for the same falling snacks.

collector_significance: The largest connected set within a single English POP series.
connection_description: Bulbapedia lays the cards out in a staggered four-row grid: row 1 Pichu, Pikachu, Buneary, Lopunny; row 2 Raichu, Pachirisu, Buizel; row 3 Piplup, Croagunk (shifted one column right); row 4 Turtwig, Chimchar (same offset). Shared edges continue the scene.
description: Eleven of POP Series 9's cards, all by Midori Harada, assemble into one large festive picture of Sinnoh-era favourites and the Pikachu line.
hidden_details: The staggered layout means some cards only join on one or two sides.
storytelling: A crowd of cute Pokemon gathered together for a celebration.

collector_significance: Triumphant dual LEGEND.
connection_description: 99/102 top, 100/102 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Darkrai and Cresselia share one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
hidden_details: Reprinted in the 2026 30th Celebration Classic Collection (TCGdex 30th-c 019/020).
storytelling: Nightmare and dream under one moon.

collector_significance: One of the first dual-Pokemon LEGENDs; awards two Prize cards when Knocked Out.
connection_description: 90/95 top, 91/95 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Entei and Raikou share one two-Pokemon LEGEND illustration spread over a top and bottom card.
storytelling: Fire and lightning beasts charging together.

collector_significance: Debut LEGEND, from the first HGSS set; both halves must be played together.
connection_description: 111/123 is the top half and 112/123 the bottom half; the art continues across the horizontal seam and the bottom half's text box is broken up around the illustration.
description: A single full-holo Ho-Oh illustration split into a top and bottom card. Together they form one oversized LEGEND card whose art fills about three quarters of the combined space.
hidden_details: LEGEND cards are the only cards to credit the illustrator in both English and Japanese.
storytelling: Ho-Oh presented as a single towering legend spanning two cards.

cards.notes: Top half. JP: Clash at the Summit 070/080.
Bottom half. JP: Clash at the Summit 071/080.

collector_significance: Undaunted dual LEGEND.
connection_description: 87/90 top, 88/90 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Kyogre and Groudon clash in one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
storytelling: The ancient sea-versus-land rivalry of Hoenn.

collector_significance: Promo pair; Latias and Latios are among the most frequently connected duos in TCG history.
connection_description: Latias (left), Latios (right); sky and flight trails continue across the seam.
description: Latias and Latios fly together through one sky across two HGSS Black Star Promos.
storytelling: The Eon duo flying in tandem.

collector_significance: Counterpart to Ho-Oh LEGEND; one of only two single-Pokemon LEGENDs.
connection_description: 113/123 top, 114/123 bottom; the illustration joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Lugia rendered across a top and bottom LEGEND half, forming one tall full-holo illustration.
storytelling: Lugia presented as a single towering legend spanning two cards.

cards.notes: Top half. JP: Clash at the Summit 072/080.
Bottom half. JP: Clash at the Summit 073/080.

collector_significance: The last LEGEND printed in English.
connection_description: 101/102 top, 102/102 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Palkia and Dialga share one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
storytelling: The masters of space and time locked together.

cards.notes: Image from images.pokemontcg.io (hsp) - TCGdex has no image.
Image from images.pokemontcg.io (hsp) - TCGdex has no image.

collector_significance: Late HGSS promos; less commonly known pair.
connection_description: Porygon (left), Porygon2 (right); the cyber-space background continues across the seam.
description: Porygon and Porygon2 share one digital-space scene across two HGSS Black Star Promos.
storytelling: The virtual Pokemon and its upgrade together inside cyberspace.

collector_significance: Unleashed dual LEGEND.
connection_description: 92/95 top, 93/95 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Raikou and Suicune share one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
storytelling: Lightning and water beasts paired.

cards.notes: Top half. JP: Clash at the Summit 074/080.
Bottom half. JP: Clash at the Summit 075/080.

collector_significance: Undaunted dual LEGEND; strong competitive history.
connection_description: 89/90 top, 90/90 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Rayquaza and Deoxys share one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
storytelling: The sky-high clash from the Destiny Deoxys film.

collector_significance: Final card numbers of Unleashed.
connection_description: 94/95 top, 95/95 bottom; the art joins across the horizontal seam.
description: Suicune and Entei share one LEGEND illustration split across a top and bottom card.
storytelling: Water and fire beasts paired, completing the Unleashed rotation of the three beasts.

collector_significance: BW-era promo trio that is easy to miss because of the non-sequential numbers.
connection_description: Darumaka (left), Axew (centre), Scraggy (right); the stall shelving, crates and fruit continue across both seams.
description: Darumaka, Axew and Scraggy share one market-stall scene piled with fruit baskets across three BW Black Star Promos.
hidden_details: The promo numbers are not consecutive (BW18, BW26, BW25).

collector_significance: Two gold-border-era secret rares split across different expansions.
connection_description: Meowth (left), Pikachu (right); the grass, trees and sky continue across the seam.
description: The secret-rare Meowth from Noble Victories and the secret-rare Pikachu from Black & White sit in the same sunny meadow, released two sets apart.
storytelling: Team Rocket's Meowth and Ash's Pikachu - the anime's long-running rivals.

connection_description: Gothorita (left), Gothita (right); the background continues across the seam.
description: Gothorita and Gothita share one scene across two cards from the Japanese-exclusive Everyone's Exciting Battle quarter-deck collection.
storytelling: The Gothita line together.

collector_significance: Fan-catalogued pairing.
connection_description: Alternate-perspective pairing - each card shows the other Pokemon in its background; the edges do not obviously join.
description: Charmeleon and Swablu, both drawn by Akira Komayama for Legendary Treasures, appear to show the same grassy hillside from two viewpoints: a small blue bird is visible behind Charmeleon, and a small red Pokemon is visible behind Swablu.
hidden_details: Each Pokemon appears as a background cameo on the other card.
review_reason: Only source is the MyDex connected-art gallery; same artist and set, but no reputable source confirms the illustrations physically join.
storytelling: Two Pokemon noticing each other across the same field.

collector_significance: Popular fan-cited pair; cheap commons/uncommons.
connection_description: Natu (left) and Bouffalant (right) show the same moment at different zoom levels; it is a narrative link rather than a confirmed edge-to-edge join.
description: A two-card story by the same artist: the Natu card shows a pair of Natu nestled in thick fur in the snow, and the Bouffalant card pulls back to reveal they are perched in Bouffalant's afro.
review_reason: Cited by fan galleries (MyDex, CBR list) as a story pair; not listed on Bulbapedia's combined-illustration page and a physical edge join is unverified - may be same-artist narrative only.
storytelling: Natu finding a fluffy hiding place.

collector_significance: An inexpensive common pair, which makes it an easy entry point to connected-art collecting. It continues the long tradition of Plusle and Minun art designed to sit side by side.
connection_description: With Plusle on the left and Minun on the right, the street, buildings and crowd carry straight across the shared edge, and the falling confetti and pennant-strung background line up between the two cards.
description: Plusle and Minun cheer at a festive outdoor town tournament, with confetti in the air and a crowd of spectators behind them. Each card shows one of the pair grinning at the viewer, and together they make one continuous street scene.
group_name: Furious Fists Plusle & Minun Cheer Squad
hidden_details: The scene belongs to Furious Fists' wider tournament theme. Bulbapedia also lists these two in a set-wide narrative group of Pokémon battling in a town tournament with a bracket board.
storytelling: The cheering Pokémon root for the fighters elsewhere in Furious Fists, fitting the set's martial-arts tournament theme.

collector_significance: One of the few true three-card combined illustrations of the XY era and the main panoramic piece of the Japanese Legendary Shine Collection (CP2).
connection_description: The cards sit side by side in the order Regigigas, Arceus, White Kyurem. The pale diagonal light rays that fan out from the upper left run uninterrupted across all three frames, and the mossy rocks and haze along the bottom of Regigigas continue under Arceus and into the crag beneath White Kyurem.
description: Three full-art legendary promos tied to the 2015 Hoopa movie form one wide, sunlit mountainside. Regigigas stands at the left, Arceus rises in the centre bathed in shafts of light, and White Kyurem lunges forward on the right above a stormy, rocky shore. Read together they look like a single poster of the legendaries Hoopa summons in the film.
group_name: Clash of Ages Trio: Regigigas, Arceus & White Kyurem
hidden_details: The English prints were split across two products (Regigigas in the Pikachu-EX Legendary Collection, Arceus and White Kyurem in the Hoopa-EX Legendary Collection), so completing the panorama required buying both boxes.
storytelling: References Pokémon the Movie: Hoopa and the Clash of Ages, in which Hoopa's rings call up a series of legendary Pokémon to battle.

collector_significance: Part of the long-running Volbeat and Illumise tradition, where the pair appear together in the same set with the same artist; this is one of the clearest physically joined examples.
connection_description: Volbeat sits on the left and Illumise on the right. The swirling light trail curves out of Volbeat's card and continues around Illumise, and the red-roofed house cut off at Volbeat's right edge is completed at Illumise's left edge, together with the flower line along the bottom.
description: Volbeat and Illumise dance through the air in a painterly scene. A sweeping green-and-gold ribbon of light, like a firefly's glowing trail, spirals behind them over a flowered meadow, with a small red-roofed building in the distance.
group_name: Primal Clash Volbeat & Illumise Light Trail
hidden_details: The building split across the border is the clearest alignment check. Komiya's textured, impressionistic brushwork matches across both halves.
storytelling: Illumise's Pokédex lore has it guiding Volbeat's light signs, and the shared light trail shows the two drawing patterns in the sky together.

cards.notes: JP: Legendary Shine Collection (CP2) 002/027. EN release: Hoopa-EX Legendary Collection.
JP: Legendary Shine Collection (CP2) 020/027. EN release: Pikachu-EX Legendary Collection.

collector_significance: A two-card combined illustration by Mitsuhiro Arita, one of the TCG's most collected illustrators; Bulbapedia's card trivia names it as one half of a combined illustration.
connection_description: Placed Reshiram left and Black Kyurem right, the two dragons face each other across the card border. Blue lightning bolts break into the right edge of Reshiram's red background, and orange embers drift into the lower left of Black Kyurem's blue sky, so each card carries a piece of the other's element exactly where they meet.
description: Two full-art promos that together show Reshiram and Black Kyurem clashing head-on. Reshiram, wreathed in red flame, occupies the left card; Black Kyurem crackles with blue electricity on the right. The split down the middle reads as fire colliding with lightning.
group_name: Reshiram & Black Kyurem: Fire Meets Lightning
hidden_details: Like the Nagasawa trio, the halves were split across products: Reshiram in the Hoopa-EX Legendary Collection and Black Kyurem in the Pikachu-EX Legendary Collection.
storytelling: Part of the Hoopa and the Clash of Ages legendary line-up; the image stages a direct confrontation between the two Unova dragons.

collector_significance: Trainer-kit exclusives that are often overlooked. In Japan the same art was a 2015 'Hoopa's Appearance' campaign lottery prize (145/XY-P and 146/XY-P), which is much scarcer.
connection_description: With the Latias card on the left and the Latios card on the right, the two Pokémon fly side by side and the background flows across the shared edge into one illustration. Community lists describe the backdrop as yellow speed lines running continuously across both cards.
description: The headline Pokémon of the two half decks in the XY Trainer Kit are drawn as one image of the Eon duo flying together. Latias anchors one card and Latios the other, so the kit's two decks each hold half of a single scene.
hidden_details: Each half deck prints its Eon Pokémon twice (Latias at 14/30 and 30/30, Latios at 13/30 and 30/30). Bulbapedia's combined-illustration list cites the 30/30 cards.
storytelling: The two half decks are designed to be played against each other, and the joined art reunites the brother-and-sister pair when the decks are laid side by side.

collector_significance: Continues the Volbeat and Illumise combined-illustration tradition into the Sun & Moon era, as a cheap and easy-to-find uncommon pair.
connection_description: Volbeat sits on the left and Illumise on the right. The rose hedge and its foliage run straight through the shared border, and the flower colours shift from red on Volbeat's side to white on Illumise's side, so the two cards form one gradient garden.
description: Volbeat and Illumise hover over a lush rose garden under a soft sky. The hedge of blooms runs the full width of the pair, with Volbeat above deep red and pink roses and Illumise above pale pink and white ones.
group_name: Celestial Storm Volbeat & Illumise Rose Garden
hidden_details: The change in rose colour from one card to the next mirrors Volbeat's red-and-blue palette and Illumise's softer purple-and-cream one.
storytelling: Their attacks are designed to chain: Illumise's Pheromone Signals powers up Volbeat's Pheromone Catch. The joined art echoes that mechanic, since Illumise's sweet scent draws Volbeat in.

collector_significance: The Sun & Moon era's physically joined Latias and Latios pair, adding to a series of paired Eon-duo art that runs from the EX era to Scarlet & Violet. The English versions came only in the two separate Dragon Majesty pin collections.
connection_description: Latias goes on the left and Latios on the right. The rows of orange-tiled roofs, streets and hazy horizon continue across the shared edge, and the white motion streaks behind the dragons line up so they read as flying side by side through one sky.
description: Latias and Latios swoop low over a sprawling terracotta-roofed city, seen from above at speed. The two promos form one aerial cityscape with the pair flying in formation over the rooftops.
group_name: Dragon Majesty Pin Collection Latias & Latios Over the City
hidden_details: The Japanese prints were Pokémon Card Gym prize-pack promos (September to November 2018) and carry the Card Gym logo, which the English pin-collection versions lack.
storytelling: The Eon duo patrol the city they protect, a recurring idea from their film Pokémon Heroes and from earlier Latias and Latios cards.

collector_significance: Splits across a main-set common and a black star promo, so many collectors never put the two together.
connection_description: Eevee (Shining Fates 052/072) on the left, Vaporeon (SWSH072 promo) on the right. The water surface and splash trails cross the edge between the two art windows.
description: Eevee splashes along a shallow, glittering stream while Vaporeon glides through the water beside it. The watercolour-like ripples and pale sky are shared by both cards.
storytelling: Eevee meeting the water evolution it could become.

collector_significance: One of three Eeveelution-plus-Eevee combined promo pairs in the SWSH promo line.
connection_description: Flareon (SWSH041) on the left, Eevee (SWSH042) on the right. The grass, light and fire sparks flow across the edge between the art boxes.
description: Flareon bounds through warm, sunlit grass while an Eevee chases after it, an ember flicking from its tail. The two windows show one meadow.
storytelling: An Eevee following the evolution it may become.

collector_significance: Early SWSH-era promo pair. Their consecutive numbers make them easy to collect together.
connection_description: Zacian (SWSH033) on the left, Zamazenta (SWSH034) on the right. The rock cliffs and cloud line carry across the shared edge, so the pair reads as one landscape.
description: The two Galar legendary heroes stand side by side on a rocky ridge under a bright sky, Zacian with its blade-like mane and Zamazenta braced with its shield. The canyon walls and sky run behind both.
storytelling: The sword and shield legends of Galar presented as partners.

cards.notes: left (order assumed); story continues on Sandygast 125/264

collector_significance: An easily missed common/rare connection in a large set.
connection_description: Araquanid (020/264) and Mudkip (062/264) share one shoreline. The stream, wet sand and palm-lined beach run across the edge between their art windows. Shown with Araquanid on the left; the left/right order has not been checked against a source.
description: On a tropical beach, an upset Sandygast has lost some of its trinkets to the tide. Mudkip searches the shallows for them while Araquanid uses its water bubble and sand to hold back a small stream.
group_name: Araquanid and Mudkip Beach Scene (KIYOTAKA OSHIYAMA)
hidden_details: The story finishes on Sandygast (125/264), where a happy Sandygast shows off its recovered treasure. Bulbapedia treats that card as a narrative follow-up, not part of the joined art, so it is not counted here.
storytelling: A small rescue story: two Pokémon helping a third get its belongings back.

collector_significance: First released in Japan in the V-UNION Special Card Sets (Aug 2021), then in English V-UNION Special Collections (Nov 2021). Collectors chase complete four-piece sets; the boxes also held a jumbo of the assembled art.
connection_description: Four standard cards form a 2x2 grid. The name/HP bar spans the top edge of the top pair, the attacks and weakness/V-UNION rule bar span the bottom pair, and the artwork runs uninterrupted across both the vertical and horizontal seams.
description: Greninja springs across the frame in a low, twisting pose, its pink tongue scarf trailing behind it, as a spiralling vortex of water opens beside it. The figure is big enough to need all four pieces. Together the four cards make one large Pokémon V-UNION.
storytelling: A single dramatic action pose blown up to four times the usual size.

connection_description: Ho-Oh (001/025) on the left, Lugia (022/025) on the right. The gold lattice backdrop and leaves continue unbroken across the edge.
description: Ho-Oh and Lugia sit side by side in front of a decorative lattice screen surrounded by autumn foliage, one in rainbow fire tones and the other in silver-white.

connection_description: Jolteon (SWSH094) on the left, Eevee (SWSH118) on the right. The lightning bolts and starburst background continue across the join.
description: A spiky, grinning Jolteon crackles with yellow lightning while an Eevee leaps through the same electric burst beside it. The bold comic-style sparks fill both frames.
storytelling: Eevee playing in Jolteon's static.

collector_significance: First released in Japan in the V-UNION Special Card Sets (Aug 2021), then in English V-UNION Special Collections (Nov 2021). Collectors chase complete four-piece sets; the boxes also held a jumbo of the assembled art.
connection_description: Four standard cards form a 2x2 grid. The name/HP bar spans the top edge of the top pair, the attacks and weakness/V-UNION rule bar span the bottom pair, and the artwork runs uninterrupted across both the vertical and horizontal seams.
description: Mewtwo floats over a night-time city skyline washed in pink and violet psychic light, its glowing, oversized fist thrust toward the viewer. Its head and arms fill the top pair and its body and tail curl through the bottom pair. Together the four cards make one large Pokémon V-UNION.
storytelling: A single dramatic action pose blown up to four times the usual size.

collector_significance: Unlike the other V-UNIONs, it was pulled from booster packs (Japanese VMAX Climax, Dec 2021). In English it came in the Morpeko V-UNION Special Collection (Apr 2022) as SWSH215-218.
connection_description: Four standard cards form a 2x2 grid. Title bar across the top pair, attacks and the weakness/V-UNION rule bar across the bottom pair; the artwork carries over every seam.
description: Full Belly Morpeko leaps through a circular burst of rainbow-tinted electric energy above a sunny meadow of grass and yellow flowers. Arita's painting is the regular version of the Morpeko V-UNION.
storytelling: A cheerful action shot of Morpeko in its Full Belly mode.

connection_description: Four standard cards form a 2x2 grid. The V-UNION title bar and rules box run across the top pair, the attack text and the weakness/V-UNION rule bar run across the bottom pair, and Pikachu bodies are split across every internal edge so they only read whole when all four are placed together.
description: A crowd of twenty-five Pikachu tumble, wave and leap across a bright sky-blue and green burst, forming one oversized Pikachu V-UNION card. Each Pikachu was drawn by a different TCG illustrator to mark the game's 25th anniversary, so the finished picture is a sampler of 25 house styles.
hidden_details: Every Pikachu is a different artist's interpretation, including veterans such as Mitsuhiro Arita, Atsuko Nishida and Kagemaru Himeno alongside newer artists.
storytelling: An anniversary group portrait: the game's mascot as seen by the artists who drew it over 25 years.

connection_description: Reshiram (002/025) on the left, Zekrom (010/025) on the right. The swirling smoke-and-cloud background and the line of the ground continue across the shared edge between the two art windows.
description: Reshiram and Zekrom are drawn in a sepia ink-wash style as two halves of one composition set against a shared swirl of smoke and cloud.
storytelling: The yin-yang dragons of Unova, ideals and truth, joined into one image.

connection_description: Seviper (102/198) on the left, Zangoose (120/198) on the right. Seviper's tail swing and Zangoose's slash trail meet at the shared edge, completing the strike.
description: The rivals Seviper and Zangoose clash in a burst of motion. Seviper coils with its blade tail raised on one side, and Zangoose lunges with its claws in a blue slash on the other.
hidden_details: Seviper carries the Single Strike mark and Zangoose the Rapid Strike mark, so the battle art also shows the set's two fighting styles.
storytelling: The natural feud between Seviper and Zangoose, shown mid-fight.

description: Arita paints the Galar legends in their Crowned forms charging through a green, lightning-streaked storm with debris flying around them.

description: Crowned Sword Zacian dives through streaks of blue and red light with its great blade gripped in its jaws, as green leaves scatter around it. The sword cuts diagonally across the grid and is split between pieces. Together the four cards make one large Pokémon V-UNION.
storytelling: A single dramatic action pose blown up to four times the usual size.

connection_description: Each card shows part of the partner Pokémon at its outer edge, and the rocky ground and energy bursts may meet when Magmortar (020/172) and Electivire (047/172) are placed together. It may instead be two views of the same moment rather than one continuous image.
description: Magmortar and Electivire, the old Sinnoh rivals, fight side by side in a rocky arena, flames on one side and electricity on the other. Each card shows a glimpse of its partner at the edge.
review_reason: Bulbapedia lists this pair only as a narrative illustration (fighting arm in arm in a rocky setting), not as a combined illustration. A thumbnail side-by-side suggests the partners overlap at the edges, but no source confirms a seamless edge join.
storytelling: Rivals turned teammates. Their attacks also reward having the other on the bench.

collector_significance: The best-known connected set in the Sword & Shield era, and a direct ancestor of the Scarlet & Violet illustration-rare panoramas. Full nine-card sets are a popular binder and frame display.
connection_description: Arrange GG26-GG34 in numeric order as a 3x3 grid. Tree trunks, the mountain slope behind Swablu, the clouds and the ground line all run straight across each vertical and horizontal seam. The path and flower beds join along the bottom row.
description: Nine full-art cards come together as one woodland scene: a snowy peak and drifting clouds across the top row, sunlit forest in the middle, and a flower-strewn path with falling petals along the bottom. Riolu, Swablu, Duskull, Bidoof, Pikachu (sheltering under a leaf), Turtwig, Paras, Poochyena and Mareep each sit in their own part of the forest.
hidden_details: The windblown orange petals carry across every card.
storytelling: A quiet day in one forest, with each Pokémon going about its own business in a shared place.

collector_significance: Pairs a chase Special Illustration Rare with its Illustration Rare pre-evolution, so the full image requires one of the set's more expensive cards.
connection_description: Stack Gholdengo ex above Gimmighoul. The brick-wall background continues between the two, and part of Gholdengo's golden body/surfboard intrudes into the top edge of the Gimmighoul card.
description: A flat, poster-like gold-and-orange vault scene. Gholdengo poses with folded arms in front of a wall of gold bricks, and below it a Gimmighoul sits smugly inside an open treasure chest overflowing with coins.
storytelling: Shows the evolution relationship in one frame: Gimmighoul hoards coins in its chest, and Gholdengo is what it becomes once it collects enough.

collector_significance: The first of the annual "connected commons" projects (2023 HYOGONOSUKE, 2024 Teeziro, 2025 Ayako Ozaki, 2026 Saboteri). Cheap individually but easy to overlook because they are ordinary commons scattered across five sets.
connection_description: Each card's framed artwork window is one ninth of a single painting; trees, shoreline, sand and water continue across the left/right and top/bottom edges of neighbouring cards. The order shown follows the Bulbapedia listing; the cards were spread across five different expansions so the mural only assembles after collecting all of them.
description: Nine Common and Uncommon cards released across the first year of Scarlet & Violet form one sunny outdoor landscape when laid out in a 3x3 binder page. The scene runs from sky and treetops down to a sandy shore and water, with each Pokemon occupying its own patch of the larger picture, such as Palossand rising out of the sand like a sandcastle.
hidden_details: The completed artwork was later reproduced on the Japanese "Connecting World" card sleeves, which is the easiest way to see the full picture without the card frames.
set_name: Scarlet & Violet Base Set / Paldea Evolved / Obsidian Flames / Paradox Rift / Paldean Fates
storytelling: Not a narrative piece; it is an ambient snapshot of everyday Pokemon life in one location, revealed piece by piece over the year.

collector_significance: An unusual pairing where one half is a black star promo and the other a main-set Crown Zenith card.
connection_description: Pikachu V (SWSH285) on the left, Eevee V (Crown Zenith 108) on the right. The white wind arcs and floating rocks continue across the shared vertical edge.
description: Pikachu and Eevee dash side by side through swirling wind and flying rocks under a bright sky. Each card shows one of them, but the streaks of wind and scattered debris form one continuous action shot.
group_name: Pikachu V and Eevee V (You Iribi)
storytelling: Two franchise mascots racing together.

collector_significance: An Illustration Rare pair from Paradox Rift by OKACHEKE, who returned a year later for the Latios / Latias ex connection in Surging Sparks.
connection_description: Plusle sits on the left card and Minun on the right; the wooden tabletop, the couch and the people lounging on it continue across the shared edge.
description: Plusle and Minun cheer on a cosy living-room table covered in snacks, drinks and a plate of fries, sparking their pom-pom-like electricity while people relax on the couch behind them. It reads like a house party or a group watching a match together.
storytelling: The pair act as literal cheerleaders, matching their in-game role of supporting allies.

collector_significance: The chase cards of Crown Zenith. The Japanese versions are the VSTAR Universe UR golds 259-262.
connection_description: Placed in the order Palkia (GG67), Arceus (GG70), Dialga (GG68), Giratina (GG69), the golden clouds, the light beam and the dark rock formations run straight across each seam. This is not the numeric order.
description: The four gold VSTAR secret rares that close out Crown Zenith form one wide, fiery skyscape. Origin Forme Palkia, Arceus, Origin Forme Dialga and Giratina hang over a glowing, cloud-choked abyss, with Arceus rising on a pillar of light near the centre.
group_name: Sinnoh Creation Trio and Arceus Gold Panorama
storytelling: The Sinnoh creation myth: Arceus with the deities of space, time and antimatter.

collector_significance: Pairs the Ancient and Future Paradox Illustration Rares from Paradox Rift, a set built around that dichotomy.
connection_description: Place Slither Wing on the left and Iron Moth on the right; the clouds and light glow of the sky run across the shared vertical edge, shifting from sunset tones into the futuristic glow.
description: The two Paradox forms of Volcarona share one sky. Slither Wing, the ancient form, rears up against a warm prehistoric sunset with palm-like silhouettes, while Iron Moth, the future form, hovers with its burning panels spread against a cooler, glowing cosmic backdrop.
group_name: Slither Wing & Iron Moth: Past and Future Volcarona
storytelling: The split sky visualises the Paradox theme of the set: one creature from the distant past and one from the far future meeting across a single horizon.

collector_significance: One of the first connected Illustration Rare / Special Illustration Rare pairings of the Scarlet & Violet era, setting the template for the IR+SIR combinations that followed in later sets.
connection_description: Stack the Special Illustration Rare above the Illustration Rare. The tips of Spidops's long green legs run off the bottom edge of its card and reappear at the top of the Tarountula card, and the brown tree trunk on the right-hand side continues uninterrupted from one card to the other.
description: A painted woodland scene beside a river: Spidops hangs upside-down from a thick tree branch on a single strand of silk, its body framed against the leaves. Directly below, on the second card, a small Tarountula dangles over open water and sky, its own thread swaying in the breeze with leaves drifting past.
hidden_details: Tarountula's silk line curves back up toward the hunter above it, so the predator-and-prey relationship only reads once both cards are stacked.
storytelling: The pairing jokes about Spidops as a trap-setting hunter: the evolved spider waits overhead while its pre-evolution swings obliviously below.

collector_significance: Consecutive Illustration Rares (165 and 166) designed as a matched pair.
connection_description: Deerling goes on the left, Sawsbuck on the right. The pink blossom trees at Deerling's right edge flow straight into the pink canopy on Sawsbuck's left edge, and the patterned forest floor lines up across the join.
description: A stylised, colour-blocked forest in which bands of trees shift through autumn orange, winter blue, spring pink and summer green. Deerling leaps through the warm left side while Sawsbuck stands among the multicoloured trunks on the right.
hidden_details: The seasonal colour bands reference Deerling and Sawsbuck's seasonal forms from the games.
storytelling: A walk through all four seasons from a young Deerling to a fully grown Sawsbuck.

collector_significance: Among the first cards revealed for Surging Sparks and promoted as connected art; links an Illustration Rare to a chase Special Illustration Rare.
connection_description: Latios goes on the left and Latias ex on the right. The cloudbank, the sunlit sea and the city skyline continue across the join so the two dragons share one horizon, with Latias angled back toward her brother.
description: The Eon duo glide over a coastal city at golden hour. Latios soars high on the left against towering sunset clouds, while Latias banks close to the viewer on the right, the rooftops and sea glowing orange below them.
group_name: Latios & Latias ex: Sunset Over the City
storytelling: Sibling legendaries flying together, echoing their pairing in Pokemon Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald.

collector_significance: Pairs a Supporter Special Illustration Rare with a Pokemon Illustration Rare; listed by Bulbapedia as a combined illustration despite the point-of-view style of connection.
connection_description: The pair are two views of the same moment rather than a seamless landscape: Perrin's card shows her taking the shot, and the Growlithe card is the subject in front of her lens. Set Perrin on the left and Growlithe on the right to read photographer then photograph.
description: Perrin, the photographer from Pokemon Scarlet and Violet: The Teal Mask, raises her camera straight at the viewer in a bright, leafy setting. The Hisuian Growlithe card shows a big, happy Growlithe sprawled close to the lens in the same sun-dappled greenery.
group_name: Perrin & Hisuian Growlithe: The Photo Shoot
storytelling: A small story of a photographer and her subject, tied to Perrin's role in the DLC as someone documenting Pokemon.

collector_significance: Second annual connected-commons project. Dudunsparce is a Rare and Passimian an Uncommon; the rest are Commons, so the set is cheap but scattered across five products.
connection_description: Each card's art box is one tile of a 3x3 painting; terrain, sky and water continue across neighbouring edges. Order shown follows the Bulbapedia listing. The first card came out in Temporal Forces (March 2024) and the last (Spheal) in Surging Sparks (November 2024).
description: Nine regular cards released through 2024 combine into a single habitat landscape. Rocky ground and grassland run across the tiles, with each of the nine Pokemon placed in its own section of the terrain.
hidden_details: The full artwork was printed on the Japanese "Connecting World - Everyone's Habitat" sleeves, revealed by Pokemon Center Japan before the final card was out.
set_name: Temporal Forces / Twilight Masquerade / Shrouded Fable / Stellar Crown / Surging Sparks
storytelling: An ambient "everyone's habitat" scene rather than a plot.

collector_significance: An unusual case of regular Common cards (not Illustration Rares) designed as a connecting pair, with consecutive numbers 009 and 010.
connection_description: Volbeat on the left, Illumise on the right. The night sky, distant tree line and the flowers along the bottom of the art box continue across the shared edge.
description: Under a starry night sky with a full moon, Volbeat and Illumise float side by side above a meadow of pale flowers, dark trees framing the scene on either side.
storytelling: Reflects the species' Pokedex lore in which Illumise guides Volbeat's light displays at night.

collector_significance: The 2025 instalment of the annual connected-commons tradition, and the first to use six cards instead of nine.
connection_description: A 2-row by 3-column arrangement; foliage, walls and paths continue from each card's art box into its neighbours. Order shown follows the Bulbapedia listing.
description: Six Commons from Journey Together and Destined Rivals combine into one overgrown outdoor scene with greenery and garden structures; the sleeve release that reproduced it was titled "Secret Stairway". Paras, Lotad, Ponyta, Mankey, Buizel and Taillow each occupy a patch of the scene.
group_name: Ayako Ozaki 2025 Connected Commons: Secret Stairway
hidden_details: Reproduced in full on the Japanese "Connecting World - Secret Stairway" sleeves.
storytelling: Ambient scene; no explicit narrative.

collector_significance: The first connected IR/SIR group of the Mega Evolution era, ending in one of the base set's Special Illustration Rares.
connection_description: Laid left to right as Bulbasaur, Ivysaur, Mega Venusaur ex; the sweeping vines and petal swirls cross the card edges and carry the eye along the evolution line. (Bulbapedia confirms the three as one combined illustration; left-to-right order inferred from the evolution sequence and art.)
description: A vivid, neon-coloured jungle of swirling petals, vines and leaves. Bulbasaur leaps with its vines outstretched, Ivysaur bounds forward through the foliage, and Mega Venusaur dominates the final panel in full bloom.
group_name: Bulbasaur, Ivysaur & Mega Venusaur ex: Jungle Bloom
storytelling: Growth from seedling to Mega-evolved giant across one continuous jungle.

collector_significance: Thematically tied to the card abilities: Ninjask's Cast-Off Shell lets you search for Shedinja.
connection_description: Bulbapedia lists the two as one combined illustration. The forest foliage and light rays connect the two art boxes; the arrangement shown (Ninjask above Shedinja) is inferred from the lighting, with the sunburst at the top of Ninjask's card and the shaded canopy on Shedinja's.
description: A forest clearing pierced by a burst of sunlight. Ninjask darts through the bright, web-like rays high in the canopy, while the hollow Shedinja shell hangs in the darker, mossy undergrowth beneath it.
storytelling: Shows the Nincada split: Ninjask flies off into the light while the empty shell it left behind comes to life as Shedinja.

collector_significance: Continues the yearly tradition after HYOGONOSUKE (2023), Teeziro (2024) and Ayako Ozaki (2025). Saboteri also drew the 30th-anniversary First Partner triptych promos.
connection_description: Each card's framed art box is one tile of a larger city painting; buildings and sky continue into neighbouring tiles. Order shown follows the Bulbapedia listing and should be treated as provisional until the full layout is published.
description: The fourth annual connected-commons mural, drawn by Saboteri and spread across the Mega Evolution era sets. The pieces released so far form an urban scene with modern high-rise buildings and sky, with Fearow and its flock flying past skyscrapers and other Pokemon such as Magneton, Aipom and Bronzor placed around the cityscape.
group_name: Saboteri 2026 Connected Commons: City Skyline (in progress)
review_reason: Membership of all seven cards is confirmed by Bulbapedia (as of July 2026), but the annual project appears to be ongoing (earlier years had 6-9 cards), and the panel arrangement and final grid shape have not been confirmed. Cyclizar is so far Japanese-only.

collector_significance: Same artist as the Temporal Forces Deerling / Sawsbuck pair; the Mega Greninja ex SIR is one of Chaos Rising's headline cards.
connection_description: Laid left to right as Froakie, Frogadier, Mega Greninja ex; the rushing water and spray arcs pass across each card boundary. Left-to-right order inferred from the evolution sequence; the trio is confirmed as one combined illustration by Bulbapedia.
description: A brilliantly coloured waterside scene of splashing streams, bubbles and patterned foliage. Froakie crouches in the shallows, Frogadier springs out of a spray of water, and Mega Greninja strikes a dynamic pose in the final panel.
group_name: Froakie, Frogadier & Mega Greninja ex: Riverbank Ninja
storytelling: The evolution line progresses from a cautious Froakie to a fully Mega-evolved ninja in one sweep of water.

collector_significance: Part of the all-foil 30th Celebration set (September 2026).
connection_description: Proposed order Moltres, Articuno, Zapdos: the pastel swirls and cloud bands at the edges look designed to flow into one another, but the exact join has not been confirmed by a primary source.
description: Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres each burst out of a swirling, rainbow-tinted cloudscape painted by mashu, with icy blue, electric yellow and fiery orange dominating their respective cards. Placed together they appear to form one sky shared by the three legendary birds.
hidden_details: Each card's Ability references the other two birds being in play, mirroring the art link in gameplay.
review_reason: Only one secondary news source (pokedexia) states the three are designed to sit side by side; not yet on Bulbapedia's combined-illustration list, and the left-to-right order and exact edge joins are unconfirmed. The cards are not consecutively numbered (Lapras 131 by a different artist sits between them).
storytelling: A reunion of the Kanto legendary birds for the 30th anniversary.

connection_description: Silvally on the left, Gladion's Final Battle on the right; the streaks of light and sky behind them run across the shared edge so Gladion's command and Silvally's charge form one composition.
description: A dramatic, wind-swept battle scene under a bright sky. Silvally charges in a blur of white and blue on the left, while Gladion stands on the right, coat flaring, pointing as he directs his partner into the fight.
storytelling: Trainer and partner in a decisive battle, matching the "Final Battle" name of the Supporter.
